errors.quote: The first $b+1\le K$ rounds then act on prefix bits singly, costing $O(TpdK)$. The other $qK$ rounds see every address combination
errors.problem: The page has the round order wrong. In the paper (proof of Lemma synthetic-transform-cost) the round at $h=\ell-1$ on the long axes comes first, if there are any. The $qK$ chunk rounds $h=\ell-2,\dots,b$ come next, and the bottom prefix rounds $h=b-1,\dots,0$ come last. So the prefix rounds are not 'the first $b+1$', and there are at most $b+1$ of them ($b$ when no axis is long). The cost and error totals are unaffected.

$d$ is not free. The lemma requires $d\ge2$, $a_dp^\epsilon\le d\le b_dp^\epsilon$, $d\ell\le C_\ell p$ and $1\le K=\lfloor d^c\rfloor\le\ell-1$. The page later uses $(d-1)q=O(p/K)$, which needs $d\ell\le C_\ell p$.

errors.quote: The contraction $F^+_{\boldsymbol t}B^{-1}L^{-1}$ adds error below $\delta$
errors.problem: The exact contraction $\mathcal T_+$ adds no error: it only propagates the $2\delta+\eta$ without amplifying it. The extra $\delta$ is the computed opposite procedure's own approximation error $\|\widetilde h-\mathcal T_+\widetilde z\|$, which applies because $\widetilde z$ is a disk grid array.
